node-1.label: Patient presented with rapidly growing right scrotal swelling without local pain

node-2.label: 50-year-old Japanese man, non-smoker; medical history of hypertension treated with ARB tablet daily; no known allergies

node-3.label: Swelling developed over 3 months; no history of trauma or infections including STDs

node-4.label: Puncture at a prior hospital yielded red-colored fluid

node-5.label: Physical examination revealed swelling on the right side of the scrotum

why.why: Although painless swelling, red aspirate, and rapid growth initially raised concern for testicular/scrotal malignancy, ultrasound and MRI show a multilocular cyst with no solid lesion or contrast enhancement, and pathology reveals bland single-layer columnar epithelium with no papillary growth or stromal invasion. Immunohistochemistry is positive for epithelial markers (EpCAM, BerEP4, WT-1, ER/PR) and negative for mesothelial markers (calretinin, D2-40). These imaging, pathological, and immunohistochemical findings strongly refute malignancy.

Red aspirate and imaging showing cyst contents consistent with hematoma support a hemorrhagic scrotal collection. However, pathology demonstrates an epithelial-lined cyst rather than a primary hemorrhagic collection, and the laboratory physician explicitly refutes hemorrhagic collection as the primary diagnosis. The hemorrhagic component is best explained as hemorrhage within a benign epithelial cyst.

The absence of pain, infection, STD history, and purulent aspirate already made scrotal infection/inflammation unlikely. Imaging and pathology now demonstrate a benign epithelial cyst with hemorrhagic contents, providing a non-inflammatory explanation for the swelling and further reducing the probability of infection or inflammation.

Imaging showing a multilocular septated cyst rather than simple fluid, together with pathology demonstrating an epithelial-lined cyst, refutes simple benign scrotal fluid such as hydrocele. The red aspirate and rapid 3-month course also argue against a simple fluid collection, so confidence remains low.

node-10.label: Ultrasound and MRI show a multilocular cystic lesion with septa attached to the testis, no solid nodules, and no contrast enhancement

node-11.label: Imaging shows cyst contents consistent with hematoma

node-12.label: Pathology shows bland single-layer columnar epithelium with no mucin, papillary growth, or stromal invasion

node-13.label: Immunohistochemistry: EpCAM(+), BerEP4(+), WT-1(+), ER/PR(+), calretinin(−), D2-40(−)

node-14.label: Benign epithelial cyst (e.g., cystadenoma) with hemorrhage

attrs.why: Ultrasound/MRI demonstrate a multilocular cystic lesion attached to the testis with no solid component or enhancement; pathology reveals bland single-layer columnar epithelium without papillary growth or stromal invasion; immunohistochemistry shows epithelial markers positive and mesothelial markers negative. These concordant imaging, pathological, and immunohistochemical findings, supported by the pathologist and laboratory physician, indicate a benign epithelial cyst such as cystadenoma with hemorrhage, and refute malignancy and primary hemorrhagic collection.
